scope_gaps.note: The title reads as routine checking of sessions, app permissions and mail forwarding; the source is a recovery guide for an account that has been hacked and mentions neither session lists, app permissions nor routine review.
Source covers logging devices and apps out after a hack, not reviewing lists of sessions or connected apps.
Source ties log-out of devices and apps to account recovery after a password change, not to removing merely unneeded access.

The source frames its steps as 'if your account has been hacked' (after signs of unauthorised activity); the item widens the trigger to suspicion of takeover. Judged covered by the source's own 'how to tell if you've been hacked' section, but the source does not say it in those words. Also, the source is UK guidance and gives no service-specific or Polish procedure.
A reader might assume NCSC treats these signs as proof of compromise; the source only lists them as things to look out for.
The 'alone does not decide' caveat is not stated by the source, only implied by its framing of strange locations as things to look out for.
